blocks.name: 4-Week Foundation Block

weeks.label: Foundation
weeks.focus: Learn the hinge and squat patterns with kettlebells at 2 to 3 reps in reserve on every set. Establish the Monday, Wednesday, Friday rhythm and record the baselines.

weeks.label: Foundation +
weeks.focus: Same movements. Move to a slightly heavier bell only on exercises where every rep last week was controlled. Soreness should be fading, not building.

weeks.label: Build
weeks.focus: The main work runs as three supersets of two exercises. Dead hangs, bench dips, and hollow holds enter. The barbell Romanian deadlift arrives, empty or lightly loaded. Kettlebell swings unlock only if the hinge looks solid.

weeks.label: Consolidate
weeks.focus: Hold week 3 loads and sharpen form. Add a little time to the hangs and holds. Finish every session feeling strong, then retest the baselines at the end of the week.

blocks.intro: A phase-in month for a strong, generally fit body that has not been under a barbell or kettlebell program in a while. Years of ski racing built powerful quads; this block deliberately balances that with posterior chain and back work: deadlifts, Romanian deadlifts, rows, carries, hangs, and direct trunk work, because a desk job and a quad-dominant history both leave the back of the body underfed. Each session is one warm-up circuit, three supersets of two exercises, and a short paired cool-down, about 45 minutes door to door. Rowing is warm-up only in this version. The goal of the month is not to lift heavy. It is to finish with clean patterns, a resilient back, and room to progress into the next block.
rules: Every set ends with 2 to 3 reps left in the tank. This month is for learning patterns, not testing strength.
Supersets: alternate the two exercises in each pair with 45 to 60 seconds of rest between efforts. Three rounds of the pair, then move to the next superset.
Three sessions a week with at least one full rest day between them. If a session is missed, shift the week; never stack two training days back to back to catch up.
Move up in kettlebell weight only when every rep of every set was controlled at the target reps. "Felt easy" is a green light for next week, not for the next set.
The barbell Romanian deadlift stays light all month. An empty bar is plenty for many people at first; two kettlebells work if the bar feels heavy.
Dead hangs: shoulders pulled down away from the ears, no shrugging, feet on a box assisting as much as needed. Build time, not swing.
Bench dips stay shallow: elbows to about 90 degrees, shoulders down and back, hips close to the bench. Any front-of-shoulder pinch means swap in incline push-ups that day.
Sharp pain, especially in the low back, ends that movement for the day. Substitute the easier variation listed and make a note.
Soreness that changes how you walk means the next session runs lighter, not skipped.
recovery: Protein at every meal, with emphasis on the meal after training. A palm-sized portion or more per meal is a good anchor without counting anything.
Sleep 7.5 hours or more. Strength at this stage is built between sessions, not during them.
Hamstring and glute soreness early in the block is normal and fades. Low back tightness that lingers past a day is the signal to lighten the next hinge day.
The stretch and foam-roll session is optional but pays off: after training or on rest days, tissue warm, never forced.
Off days are for easy movement: walks, easy spins, gentle stretching. Nothing that leaves you sore.
tests: Goblet squat: bell weight that feels controlled for 8 reps
Ring row: body angle for 8 clean reps (note where the feet are)
Dead hang: longest single hang, in seconds

rest.label: Rest
rest.note: Easy movement is welcome; hard effort is not.

warmup.title: Warm-up
warmup.subtitle: Every training day · before the main work

items.name: Easy row
items.detail: 4 min at a fully conversational effort.

items.name: Bodyweight squat
items.detail: Slow down, quick up, chest tall.

items.name: Band pull-apart
items.detail: Arms straight, squeeze the shoulder blades, band to the chest.

items.name: Unloaded hip hinge
items.detail: Dowel on the back or hands on hips; push the hips back to a hamstring stretch, flat back throughout.

items.name: Leg swings + arm circles
items.detail: Front-to-back leg swings per leg, big slow arm circles both directions.

items.name: Kettlebell deadlift
items.detail: Bell between the feet, hips back, flat back, stand tall. The pattern of the whole month.

byWeek.2: 3×8, slightly heavier bell only if every week 1 rep was controlled.

items.name: Barbell Romanian deadlift
items.detail: Bar slides down the thighs to the deepest flat-back range, then hips drive forward. Pattern quality over load; an empty bar or two kettlebells is plenty.

items.name: Dead hang
items.detail: From the pull-up bar or rings. Shoulders down away from the ears, feet assisting on a box as needed. Grip, shoulders, and a gentle decompression between hinge sets.

byWeek.4: 3 × 30 s, less foot assist if it feels easy.

items.name: Single-arm kettlebell row
items.detail: Free hand braced on the rack or a bench, flat back, pull the bell to the hip.

items.name: Glute bridge
items.detail: Squeeze at the top for a full second; ribs down, no low-back arch.

byWeek.3: 3×8 per side, single leg. Hips stay level; drive through the heel.

items.name: Ring row
items.detail: Body in one line, squeeze the shoulder blades, pull the rings to the ribs. Walk the feet forward to make it harder, back to make it easier.

byWeek.3: 3×8–10, lower the body angle a step.

items.name: Dead bug
items.detail: Low back gently pressed to the floor the entire time. Slow, opposite arm and leg.

liftb.title: Lift B
liftb.subtitle: Squat + press · legs, shoulders, upper back

items.name: Goblet squat
items.detail: Bell at the chest, elbows inside the knees at the bottom, chest tall.

byWeek.2: 3×8, heavier bell if week 1 was controlled.

items.name: Bench dips
items.detail: Hands on the bench edge behind you, feet on the floor, knees bent to start. Lower until the elbows reach about 90 degrees, shoulders down and back, hips brushing the bench. Straighten the legs over the weeks to add load; any shoulder pinch means incline push-ups instead.

byWeek.4: 3×8–10, legs straighter if the shoulders feel good.

items.name: Kettlebell reverse lunge
items.detail: Step back, knee toward the floor with control, drive up through the front heel. Balance work for a ski racer's side-to-side symmetry.

byWeek.1: 3×6 per leg, bodyweight or a light bell held goblet style.
byWeek.3: 3×8 per leg, add or increase the bell.

items.name: Band face pull
items.detail: Band anchored at eye level on the rack; pull to the face with elbows high and wide. Desk-job antidote.

items.name: Loaded carry
items.detail: Tall posture, no leaning, about 20 yards per trip.

byWeek.1: 3 trips, farmer carry: a bell in each hand.
byWeek.3: 3 trips per side, suitcase carry: one bell, switch sides each trip; resist the sideways lean.
byWeek.4: 3 trips per side, suitcase carry, heavier bell if posture stays tall.

items.name: Bird dog
items.detail: Opposite arm and leg, hips level, slow. Reach long rather than high.

items.name: Kettlebell Romanian deadlift
items.detail: Bell slides down the thighs with a 2 to 3 second lowering; soft knees, flat back, hamstring stretch at the bottom.

items.name: Kettlebell deadlift
items.detail: Heavier than the weeks 1 and 2 bell; every rep crisp.

items.name: Incline push-up
items.detail: Hands on the rack safety bar. Body in one rigid line; lower the bar setting over time, not the standards.

items.name: Band good morning
items.detail: Band over the shoulders and under the feet; hinge against it with a flat back.

items.name: Kettlebell swing
items.detail: Only if the hinge looks solid. Hips snap, arms relax, bell floats to chest height. Otherwise repeat band good mornings.

items.name: Dead hang
items.detail: Second dose of the week. Shoulders down, quiet body, feet assisting as needed.

items.name: Hollow hold
items.detail: Low back pressed to the floor, arms by the sides or reaching past the hips, legs as low as the low back allows. Bend the knees to make it easier; never let the low back peel up.

items.name: Side plank
items.detail: Elbow under the shoulder, hips tall in one line. From the knees if needed.

items.name: Standing forward fold
items.detail: Soft knees, hang heavy, breathe.

items.name: Hip flexor stretch
items.detail: Half-kneeling, glute of the down leg squeezed, gentle shift forward. The desk-chair counter-move.

items.name: Child's pose
items.detail: Knees wide, arms long, let the back breathe.

items.name: Chest opener
items.detail: Forearm on the rack upright, step gently through until the chest stretches.

roll.title: Stretch + foam roll (optional)
roll.subtitle: After any session, or on rest days

items.name: Quads and hip flexors
items.detail: Slow passes, pause on tender spots, keep breathing.

items.name: Glutes and hamstrings
items.detail: Sit on the roller, tip to each side; then the back of the thighs.

items.name: Upper back
items.detail: Roller across the shoulder blades, hands behind the head, gentle extension. Stay off the low back and neck.

items.name: Calves and lats
items.detail: Optional extras if anything feels tight.

items.name: Hamstring strap stretch
items.detail: Lying on the back, band or strap over the foot, leg toward the ceiling, knee soft.

items.name: Figure-4 stretch
items.detail: Ankle over the opposite knee, pull the legs in gently. Glutes and hips.

items.name: Walk
items.detail: 20 to 30 minutes at a genuinely easy pace, outside if the weather allows.

items.name: Gentle stretch
items.detail: A few minutes for whatever feels tight: hamstrings, hips, chest. Nothing forced.
